3. That the case of the plaintiffs-opposite parties in brief are that Pandit Chandra Rudra Paul and Swarup Chandra Paul were original owners of the suit land of schedule No. 1 and while they were possessing and enjoying the property Kushai Chandra Das and Aswini Kumar Das purchased the same from them and became the owner and possessor of the land. Aswini Kumar Das died leaving behind 4 sons Ambika Charan Das, Paresh Das, Animesh Das and Amalesh Das and Kushai Chandra Das died leaving behind 2 sons Anil Chandra Das and Monindra Chandra Das and accordingly, RS Khatian No. 43 was prepared in their name. Ambika Charan Das and others while they were possessing and enjoying the property in the year 1963 they exchanged the said land with the land of one Moulavi Abdul Matin of Kasharmara Mouza of Police Station Radhakishorepur of Tripura, India and in this way Abdul Ma tin became owner and possessor of the schedule land. Moulvi Abdul Ma tin while owning and possessing the land on 28-12-64 exchanged .39 acres of land with plaintiff No. 1 and her husband Badsha Mia became owner and possessor of the same. In this way the plaintiff became owner of 0.39½ acres i.e. 0.39½ acres by exchange and 0.15 acres by purchase and thereafter sold 0.20 acres to plaintiff No. 2 who remained owner and possessor of rest 0.14½ acres of land. 

 6. The defendant Nos. 2(Ka)-2(Ja) also contested the suit by filing separate written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint stating, inter alia, that the defendant No. 2 Moulvi Deen Mohammad was a great Alem, he was the Khalifa of Sonakanda Darbar who had many disciples, the plaintiffs' predecessor Badsha Mia was also a Murid of defendant No. 2 and sold the land to defendant No. 2 by a registered deed No. 6699 dated 25-11-68 and on the same date executed a registered compensation deed No. 6700. Consequently, the defendant No. 2 during his lifetime had been living in the suit land by erecting houses and lived therein with his family and also established a Madrasha set up tube-well, latrine, etc. When the defendant No. 1 claimed the suit land and filed the Title Suit No. 78 of 1988 against the original owners, the defendant No. 2 filed a solehnama to get a compromise decree then the aforesaid compromise decree was passed. The plaintiff's predecessors Badsha Mia had no right title and possession in the suit land and in the recent survey operation when surveyor found defendant No. 2 in the suit land he prepared RS Khatian in his name correctly and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.
